text:
maria: quick thought — can we add an explicit "binding.namespace" field to rollout metadata so clients can deterministically check visibility without parsing labels? :thinking:

alex: aren't labels flexible enough? what client behavior are we trying to guarantee?

maria: labels are ambiguous for offline/client-side checks. we want clients to answer: "does this pin apply to tenant X?" with a fast exact-match, no control-plane call. labels are freeform and collide.

sam: +1 for a first-class field. makes validation and SDK helpers simpler.

kai: semantics proposal: binding.namespace is either empty (global), an opaque tenant token (ns_...), or a logical namespace id. clients should do exact equality matches. resolution precedence: tenant-token > namespace-id > global.

alex: security caveat — embedding clear tenant ids in public metadata leaks tenant existence. public APIs should return opaque namespace tokens; private control-planes can use clear text.

maria: agreed. control-plane will map tenant-id -> opaque token for public endpoints. that avoids enumeration while still enabling client checks.

sam: migration plan idea:
1) add optional binding.namespace (nullable)
2) expose opaque namespace tokens on public catalog endpoints
3) grace period (2 weeks): clients prefer namespace when present but still fall back to legacy label semantics if namespace absent
4) after window, deprecate label-based checking and require namespace match

kai: edge case: if tenant revokes a pin but a global pin also exists, do we allow implicit fallback? that seems like it violates tenant intent. recommend pins include a state {active|disabled|revoked} and clients treat disabled/revoked as explicit no-match.

alex: tie-breakers: if multiple pins match at the same specificity level, pick newest created_at, then deterministic lexical fallback by model_ref. document this in the SDK resolver.

ops-bot: feature-flag scheduled: "binding.namespace" control-plane API field enabled Wed 02:00 UTC, canary 10% tenants.

maria: i'll draft the schema PR and sample resolver pseudocode for SDK READMEs. also let's add telemetry pin_match_scope{global,tenant,namespace} and pin_resolution_outcome{matched,explicitly_disabled,fallbacked}.

sam: add an SDK linter rule to warn about label-only pin logic during migration. helps users adopt the field.

maria: thanks all — i'll post the PR + docs link when ready.
